correctness.rationale: The Finding is correct. The translated conditional simplex gives the exact covariance m(1-t)^m[B_m(b)-b H_m/m], with B_m(b)=E[(b-(M-Y_1))_+]. The labeled-coordinate joint event has volume (1-kb)_+^(m-1)/(k+1), including dimension two by direct one-coordinate integration on the nonempty interval. Inclusion–exclusion and integration give the displayed finite formula. B_m(b)/b increases strictly from 1/m to 1, since there is positive mass of M-Y_1 in every (0,b), and H_m/m lies strictly between. At t=1/2 the conditional mean is (m+1)/(2m), equal to H_m/m only at m=2 and larger thereafter, giving the claimed endpoint comparison. Under exponential normalization, the exact unnormalized gap law is e^v[1-(1-e^-v)^m]/m. Concentration of the sum gives uniform relative asymptotics e^v/m up to C log log m without needing independence of gap and sum. Integration and the two-sided bracket give s=mb_m asymptotic to log log m, then e^s-1=(1+o(1))sH_m gives the second log and additive o(1); replacing b_m by t_m costs o(1) on the scaled threshold. The adjacent wording about piecewise polynomials is imprecise: B_m is piecewise polynomial in b, whereas the covariance itself is piecewise polynomial in t and piecewise rational in b. Independent finite replay: python3 /workspace/check_frozen_mathematics.py 2, with 234 exact rational comparisons to a joint-tail inclusion–exclusion integral for m=2 through 14. This does not certify uniqueness or the asymptotic; those follow analytically.
